transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I'm not really used to talking about this, but... I guess things have just felt wrong lately. 

I'm a teaching assistant, and... well, the thing that scares me the most right now is... when I walk across campus, it's like... I don't know. It feels like I'm watching everything through glass. Like I'm not fully in my own body. The buildings and the students just... they seem kind of unreal. 

So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you feel like you're having emotions normally, or do they feel distant or muted to you?

Um... I suppose they feel muted. It's... hard to explain. 

Like, my husband cut some flowers from the garden recently. And he tried to make me tea. I knew it was a kind thing to do, but... I don't know. I just couldn't feel the warmth or pleasure I normally would. It was just... this blank heaviness.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people cannot?
No... no, nothing like that. Just... what I mentioned before.
How long have you been feeling like things are unreal and your emotions are muted?
Um... it's been... about six days. Ever since... well, there was an accident during the showcase. The lighting rig collapsed. So... since then, I guess.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the accident?

I suppose so. Um... little noises just... get to me now. 

If a door bangs, or... if a cart rattles in the hallway at work... I jump. So hard my chest actually hurts. And... I don't know, it just takes me several minutes to stop shaking and get back to what I was doing.
Have you been avoiding any places, people, or activities since the accident?

I guess so. Um... I've been taking the long way around campus. Just... so I don't have to pass the atrium. And if anyone brings up the showcase, I... I usually just change the subject. Or I make an excuse to leave before I have to talk about it.
Do you have any gaps in your memory about the accident or the time since it happened?
Um... no. Not that I've noticed. I remember what happened.
Has your daily life or relationships been significantly affected by how you've been feeling since the accident?

I guess so. Work has been... difficult. 

I actually walked out of a planning meeting the other day. I just... had to leave. And I've missed a couple of mentoring sessions with my students. Plus, like I said, I'm avoiding parts of campus that I really need to use for my job, so... yeah. It's definitely affecting things.
Are there any specific memories or thoughts about the accident that you've been trying to avoid thinking about?
Um... I don't think so. I just... I try not to dwell on it in general. But it's not like there's one specific thing I'm trying to block out. I just... prefer not to think about it at all.
Are there any activities or situations that you've been avoiding because they remind you of the accident?

Well... like I mentioned earlier, I've been taking the long way around campus. Just... so I don't have to pass the atrium. And... I guess if anyone brings up the showcase, I usually just try to change the subject. Or I find an excuse to leave before I have to talk about it. I just... I'd rather keep my distance from all that.
Do you feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body at times?

Um... yeah, I guess. It's... it's actually the part that scares me the most. Sometimes when I'm walking across campus, it's like... I don't know, like I'm watching everything through glass. It just feels like I'm not fully in my own body. And the buildings and the students... they just seem slightly unreal. It's hard to explain.
Do you feel like you're reliving the accident when you're in situations that remind you of it?

Um... I guess so. It's... well, sometimes I'll just be grading papers or making coffee, and... the sound of the rig crashing down just kind of forces its way into my head. And then... I don't know, it's like I can see the volunteer lying there, and all the students rushing forward. It feels... it feels like it's happening right then, all over again.
How often would you say you feel like you're watching everything through glass or not fully in your own body?

Um... I don't know exactly. Like I said before, it mostly just happens when I'm walking across campus. Whenever I have to be out there and the buildings and people start looking unreal like that. Maybe... a few times a week? I don't really keep count. I just try to get through it and get back inside.
How intense is the feeling of being unreal or disconnected from your body when it happens?

Um... it's pretty intense, I guess. Like I mentioned, it's the part that scares me the most. Just... that feeling of not being in my body, and everything looking so unreal. It's... it's hard to deal with.
Are there any specific physical sensations or feelings that you try to avoid because they remind you of the accident or make you feel anxious?

Um... I'm not really sure about specific physical feelings. I just... I try to avoid things that make me feel that way. 

Like... I've been taking the long way around campus lately, just so I don't have to walk past the atrium. And... if anyone brings up the showcase, I usually just change the subject. Or I find an excuse to leave before I have to talk about it. I just... I don't want to be around it.
Are there any physical sensations that you experience that make you want to avoid certain situations or places?

Um... no, I don't think so. Like I just said, I don't really notice any... specific physical feelings. I just know I don't want to go near there. I don't really pay attention to what my body is doing, I just... stay away.
Are there any thoughts or memories related to the accident that you've been trying to push away or avoid thinking about?
Um... not really any specific thoughts, I guess. I just... try not to think about it at all. If a memory pops up, I just... find something else to do. I don't really dwell on it.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family since the accident?
Um... no, not really. Things are pretty much the same. I just... I keep to myself a bit more, maybe, but no real problems.
